title: Full Inseparability and Genuine Multipartite Entanglement Coincide for Finite-Mode Gaussian States
authors: Yu Yang, Yuhang Wang, Chunxiao Du, Shikun Zhang, Zheng Qin, Rui Li, Wenxiu Li, Hao Zhang, Zhisong Xiao
abstract: For general mixed states, entanglement across every bipartition need not imply genuine multipartite entanglement (GME), because a biseparable decomposition may switch the separable cut from term to term. We prove that this convex ambiguity disappears for Gaussian states of finitely many bosonic modes. More generally, for any finite family of partitions, a Gaussian density operator in the trace-norm-closed convex class generated by states separable across those partitions is already separable across one fixed partition in the family. Only the target is Gaussian; a valid decomposition may be continuous and may contain arbitrary non-Gaussian states. Thus full inseparability and GME coincide, Gaussian k-separability and k-producibility reduce to fixed-partition tests, and party-wise tensor powers cannot activate GME from a biseparable Gaussian state. The proof combines a spectral selector with a holomorphic rigidity argument that converts one product vector in the square-root range of a Gaussian state into a block-local covariance certificate. The result shows that partition mixing, a generic mixed-state mechanism, adds no new exact finite-mode Gaussian states.
summary: This theoretical paper proves a significant rigidity result for finite-mode Gaussian states, showing that the complex concept of full inseparability is mathematically equivalent to Genuine Multipartite Entanglement (GME). The authors achieve this by employing advanced techniques from functional analysis and quantum information theory, demonstrating that the structure of Gaussian states prevents entanglement from being activated by mixing over multiple potential separable cuts.
main_problem: The paper investigates whether full inseparability (entanglement across every bipartition) and Genuine Multipartite Entanglement (GME) coincide for finite-mode Gaussian states, especially when considering convex decompositions over multiple partitions.
main_result: For finite-mode Gaussian states, the authors prove that full inseparability and GME are equivalent, demonstrating that partition mixing adds no new exact Gaussian states.
method: The proof combines spectral selection techniques with holomorphic rigidity arguments, relating local product structures in the state's spectral range to global separability conditions.
model_or_system: The study focuses on finite-mode Gaussian states of bosonic modes distributed among multiple parties. Separability is analyzed using the trace-norm-closed convex hull of product projectors ($	ext{Sep}_F$).
key_observables: Covariance matrices, entanglement depth, fixed-partition separability criteria (LMIs), and the existence of product vectors in the square-root range of the state.
important_parameters: Finiteness of modes and parties; the exponent $s$ used in Gaussian powers ($ho^s$); the specific structure of the Gaussian state.
main_assumptions: The target density operator is assumed to be an *exact* finite-mode Gaussian state. The analysis is restricted to finite numbers of parties and modes.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates convex partition rigidity for a three-party system, showing Gaussian members of $	ext{Sep}_F$ are constrained to a single fixed-partition set. Figure 2 outlines the proof roadmap involving Gaussian powers and product-range rigidity.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the general rigidity theorem for Gaussian states ($	ext{G} \cap 	ext{Sep}_F = 	ext{G} \cap  igcup 	ext{Sep}_\pi$), then applies this to the bipartition case to prove the equivalence between full inseparability and GME, relying on spectral selection and holomorphic rigidity.
why_interesting: This work provides deep structural constraints on entanglement for Gaussian states, which are highly relevant in quantum optics and continuous-variable quantum information processing, by showing that complex mixed-state entanglement measures collapse to simpler, fixed-partition tests.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Convex partition rigidity for a three-party illustration with F = {A|BC, B|AC, C|AB}. Mixing states that are separable across different cuts enlarges the unrestricted mixed-state class. Theorem 1 says that the added region has empty intersection with the finite-mode Gaussian state set: every Gaussian member of SepF already belongs to one fixed-partition separable set. The picture is schematic and the theorem holds for any finite family of partitions of finitely many finite-mode parties.

FIG. 2. Proof roadmap for Theorem 1. (a) Gaussian powers and the spectral selector produce a product vector in a square-root range. Product-range rigidity fixes a separable partition for each power; finiteness of F and trace-norm closure then fix one partition for the target. (b) The local rigidity mechanism: operator domination gives a Gaussian Husimi-Q envelope, holomorphic product contact yields a block-local pure covariance W ⪯V , and correlated displacements reconstruct a state separable across the same partition.
